title.narrative: DUF Youth Culture and Diversity - Danish-Arab Partnership Programme 2017-2022

description.narrative:
The strategic programme objective of the Danish-Arab Partnership Programme is to provide economic opportunities by advancing governance standards in public institutions, civil society and businesses.
The programme has six engagements under the two thematic programmes 1) Governance Standards and 2) Economic Opportunities. With the aims of enhancing Governance Standards for rights-holders and duty-bearers in the areas of Human Rights, Gender Equality, and Free Media. And increase the Economic Opportunities for young people, by strengthening flexible labour markets, decent jobs, and social dialogue, as well as employment opportunities, youth participation and financial engagement through youth entrepreneurship.

title.narrative: Output 1.3 Young women and men in Egypt, Jordan and Tunisia implement community-building initiatives, with support from a pool for small-scale projects, which aim to influence duty bearers, include marginalized youth in local communities, and increase dialogue and diversity

Young women and men in Egypt, Jordan and Tunisia implement community-building initiatives, with support from a pool for small-scale projects, which aim to influence duty bearers, include marginalised youth in local communities, and increase dialogue and diversity.
The community building initiatives are run solely by young volunteers, and have focus on engaging youth in activism locally in innovative formats focused on local needs assessments.
A small-scale project pool is managed by Les Scouts Tunisiens, WE Center and DEDI.

title.narrative: Strategic Youth Activities

Through innovative approaches and methods, young women and men have gained strengthened capacity to act as democratic agents of change and diversity in Egypt, Jordan and Tunisia.
A minimum of 15.000 young women and men have gained specific skills, tools and knowledge that enables them to 1) contribute to a culture of inclusion and diversity, and 2) lead and engage in efforts that contribute to a youth culture of active citizenship.
Measured through young people educated as social entrepreneurs, democratic change agents, ambassadors for dialogue and young people implementing small-scale initiatives or participating in dialogue trainings.
